paper.title_en: Two Faint Tidal Disruption Events Discovered in a Pilot Search with the Wide Field Survey Telescope
paper.abstract_en: We report the discovery of TDE 2025alrm/WFST250129blnve and TDE 2025amkg/WFST251021dbmwk in the first six months of the wide-field survey (WFS) performed by the 2.5-meter Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST). Both events are apparently faint among known optical tidal disruption events (TDEs), with peak magnitudes of $g \sim 20.0$ and $g \sim 19.6$, respectively. Blackbody fits to the multi-band photometry yield roughly constant temperatures of $\sim 10^{4}$ K for both sources, with peak bolometric luminosities of $10^{43.6}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $10^{43.8}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. Optical spectra obtained during the declining phase display characteristic broad Balmer, He II, and N III emission lines, classifying both sources as H+He TDEs. Host-galaxy SED fitting suggests stellar masses on the order of $10^{9} M_{\odot}$ and black hole masses of $\sim10^{6} M_{\odot}$, which are typical of optically selected TDE hosts. The pilot discovery of these two faint TDEs along with dozens of candidates, demonstrates the capability of WFST to discover TDEs, owing to its exceptional survey depth. Furthermore, these events highlight the value of the $u$ band in multi-band surveys for TDE selection, particularly for distinguishing TDEs from supernovae at early phases. With continued operations, WFST is expected to substantially expand the known TDE population, especially by uncovering nearby low-luminosity events and high-redshift TDEs, both of which remain poorly explored.
